title: ATLAS: A Self-Supervised and Cross-Stage Netlist Power Model for Fine-Grained Time-Based Layout Power Analysis
problem: Accurate power prediction for new designs requires time-consuming back-end processing and commercial tool simulation; delays design optimization cycles and prevents rapid power-driven exploration.
motivation: Early power estimation at netlist stage with layout accuracy could enable fast design exploration and optimization, but existing methods lack cross-design generalization or time-based simulation accuracy.
method: ATLAS employs pre-training and fine-tuning paradigm customized for circuit power. Uses self-supervised learning to predict ultimate layout-stage power from gate-level netlist without layout information. Targets golden per-cycle power from commercial simulation tools, handling separate prediction for clock tree, registers, and combinational logic.
key_novelty: First cross-design time-based power model achieving near-layout accuracy from netlist with no layout information via domain-customized deep learning.
contributions: MAPE of 0.58% (clock tree), 0.45% (register), 5.12% (combinational) with <1% total design power MAPE
Inference speed significantly faster than commercial tools
Generalizes across designs without requiring layout data

metrics.other: MAPE <1% for total power, 0.58%/0.45%/5.12% per component

limitations: Not discussed; applicability to advanced technology nodes or unusual circuit topologies unclear.
primary_theme: Self-supervised cross-design power modeling from netlist
